title.narrative: Reintegration Support for Returnee Migrant Workers of Faridpur District in Bangladesh

description.narrative: Bangladesh is one of the foremost labour-exporting countries in the world with 7.84 million male and female workers travelling to various countries from Bangladesh toAugust 2022. Remittances increased 12% to $7.63 billion from January 2022 until August 2022. Despite some successful migration, many migrants return to Bangladesh without finances promised to them, having survived abuse and exploitation by business owners and brokers, and international brokers and traffickers. In order to earn foreign currency, migrants seek employment in countries outside of Bangladesh. Most are not able to ensure safe migration due to a lack of awareness and information. In many cases, potential migrants fall victim to fraud perpetrated by local brokers through payment of fabricated job and visa processing fees. As many families commit their savings to find the finance required for migration, if survivors1 of modern slavery and vulnerable migrants2return empty-handed, they are driven further into poverty with limited employment options, and often forced to sell remaining land or houses or valuable property. There are several interventions in Bangladesh targeting short-term and long-term needs of survivors and vulnerable migrants. However, many tend to be very localised without much likelihood of having a disruptive effect on the drivers of forced labour. Many also exclude men from receiving support. Government and other NGOs run programs but they do not meet the scale of the need. This project will increase employment/self-employment and income of returnee migrants through providing vocational and short duration trainings. Returning migrants will be referred through networks to Government provision of safety net facilities, loans and job placements from governmental organisations and non-governmental organisations.
